questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've heard from other students from Copenhagen University that University of Melbourne is a great University with high academic teaching, which was the main reason for choosing to do an exchange in Melbourne.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I've found that the level of two of the subjects I attended was very high and most of the other students had a bachelor that was related to the subjects. That made it very challenging for me, due to the fact that I had no previous knowledge about the subjects.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes, and if I needed more information Stop1, which is the University's student council, was very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received several e-mails from the exchange coordinator, which was very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I already had a place before going so I would not know.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Currently im living in a sharehouse in Brunswick, which is one of the suburbs of Melbourne. It seems to be cheaper than the accommodation in the center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would not know because I already had a place before I went here.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I'm not quite sure.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Stop1 and the exchange coordinators

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Not to succesful. 
Firstly, I had all my classes accepted by the University, but then a few weeks before I got told that two of the subjects were not available. This meant that I had to choose two other courses, which was a bit of a shame because I was very excited about the other two.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's a long process so you have to be patient :-)

questions.answer: Most of the lectures were very passionate but I did miss having more discussions.

questions.answer: Go to Tasmania - so much to see! or visit national parks.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It has been pretty easy. People are very open and easy to talk to.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Because people from Melbourne are so open also it means that it can be rather hard becoming close with people living here.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is a great cultural city with a lot of events, concerts and other cultural arrangements. So the options of having great cultural experiences are definitely there!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is a very expensive city so save up a lot of money before you go!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The workload is way bigger at Melbourne University compared to Copenhagen University.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not using too much money.
